gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-17 Amazon US sells the Asustor Flashstor 6 Gen2 (FS6806X) for $829.99, the same price as the TerraMaster F8 SSD Plus ($829.99) and $20 under the UGREEN DXP480T Plus ($849.99), which puts the only six-slot box with all-Gen4 slots under $900.
standout_why: ComputingForGeeks (cited, Amazon prices from 2026-10-19) has the FS6806X at about $980 from a third-party seller with two units left, and the F8 SSD Plus at about $765. HomelabCompass (cited, updated 2026-11-02) gives a range of 'roughly $999' for the FS6806X with no retailer named. ChatGPT's own answer shows $1,040.99 at Newegg. None of them shows the FS6806X at the F8 SSD Plus's price or under $900. ComputingForGeeks already ranks the FS6806X best overall on its lanes, so the new part is the price, and the price is what decides an under-$900 page.
decides: At $829.99 the FS6806X falls inside our under-$900 cap and costs the same as ChatGPT's top 'best value' pick, the F8 SSD Plus. ComputingForGeeks says the FS6806X's slots run Gen4 x4 to Gen4 x1, so every one is faster than its 10GbE port. The F8 SSD Plus is Gen3 x1 on every slot, so a single-drive share stops near 0.9 GB/s. That makes the FS6806X the pick for six drives or fewer. The F8 SSD Plus remains the pick only if you need 7–8 slots. The DXP480T Plus stays the pick for Thunderbolt or CPU. The F4 SSD ($299.99) and F8 SSD ($373.99) are the budget tier. Recheck the $829.99 Amazon prices before publishing, because Amazon prices move.

findings.label: M.2 lanes, measured speed and where it loses
findings.value: Slots Gen4 x4 to Gen4 x1; 1,110 MB/s read and write in RAID 5; 13.1 W idle with six SSDs
findings.source_title: Best All-Flash NVMe NAS (2026): Lanes vs 10GbE | ComputingForGeeks
findings.note: ComputingForGeeks credits the measurements to KitGuru; I did not open KitGuru. ComputingForGeeks says it loses on transcoding (no iGPU) and on Linux support: the AMD 10GbE controller needed out-of-tree patches on Debian, and the module was missing on Unraid 7.2.3.

findings.label: Why it loses
findings.value: Every slot is PCIe Gen3 x1, so a one-drive share stops near 0.9 GB/s; 19.7 W idle with eight drives
findings.source_title: Best All-Flash NVMe NAS (2026): Lanes vs 10GbE | ComputingForGeeks
findings.note: ComputingForGeeks cites Liliputing for 1,236/1,230 MB/s SMB on RAID 10. It also reports that Debian, Ubuntu and TrueNAS SCALE failed to boot fully with drives on the PCIe switch, and that the warranty is 2 years versus Asustor's 3.
